articles.title: Top performers for Monroe County Region sports on Monday, Aug. 31
articles.summary: A exchange student scores four times for Milan's soccer team against Airport; Erie Mason volleyball knocks off Summerfield and other local sports.
articles.body:
German exchange student Livius Guellmeister made an immediate impression on his new friends and teammates at Milan High School by scoring four goals in a 9-1 soccer victory over Airport on Monday, Aug. 31.

"It was a wonderful debut," Milan coach Phil Hayes said. "His plane just arrived on Friday. He had some good bonding with his teammates over the weekend."

Hayes knew Guellmeister was coming, but could not get here until after the Big Reds had played their first five games of the season.

"He's played a lot of soccer," the coach said. "I don't know what level, though."

Guellmeister's level was very high Monday, scoring nearly half of his team's goals.

Robert Gill added a goals and Wyatt Hurd came out of the goal to convert a penalty kick in the season half.

Other goals for the 3-2-1 Big Reds came from Tanner Lambers and Andrew Cruz.

Airport opened the scoring in the opening 30 seconds when Adam Ortega converted a pass from freshman Wyatt Sanders.

"That definitely caught up off guard," Hayes said. "It was a wake-up call. Sometimes you need a wake-up call."

Unfortunately for Airport, the young Jets could not follow up on that wake-up call.

"We only have 11 boys," coach Nick Suarez said. "We graduated 11 seniors form last year's team, which had our best record. It's tough to lose that many.

"This was a 2-1 game through the first 25 minutes. With our lack of depth, we are not an 80-minute team right now. We have some good sixth, seventh and eighth-graders. We knew this year would be rough."

Carson Welker, SMCC : Tallied three goals and an assist to spark a 7-0 win over Flat Rock. Aaron Fowkes, Spencer Schumate and Carson Peters each recorded a goal and assist and Stephen Ban picked up his first varsity goal. Ben Chavous posted the shutout with Aidan Cronin leading the defense.

Nathan Seisdedos-Henninger, New Boston Huron : Led a balanced attack with two goals in 7-0 win over Jefferson-Erie Mason. Matthew Hussey, Gonzalo Aragon and Parker Krause all finished with a goal and an assist. Marcos Reyna and Maverik Bazzy netted the other goals and Marton Krajcz and Dominic Lividini were credited with assists. Todd Elliott recorded the shutout. Jackson Vallie turned aside 32 shots for 1-2 Jefferson-Mason.

Trey Heaton, State Line Christian : Opened his junior season with a hat trick during an 8-0 victory over Pittsford Freedom Christian. Austin Nowak added a pair of goals, JR Hobbins rang up three assists and Steve Callejas notched a shutout in his first start in goal.

Addie Homrich, Erie Mason : Racked up 13 kills in a 25-12, 22-25, 25-14, 25-20 triumph over Summerfield. "The team showed great energy, teamwork, and determination throughout the match," Mason coach Kayle Scott said. "It was a strong start to the season." articles.title: NBA Reporter Calls Out Jonathan Kuminga’s Agent After Claims on Being Hawks’ Best Player
articles.summary: Another interview from Jonathan Kuminga’s agent has put his client back under the microscope. Aaron Turner has spent much of the offseason defending the deci...
articles.body:
Another interview from Jonathan Kuminga's agent has put his client back under the microscope. Aaron Turner has spent much of the offseason defending the decisions surrounding JK's free agency. At first, he explained why the former Warriors forward passed on more lucrative opportunities and eventually chose the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Now, Turner is defending Kuminga's brief run with the Atlanta Hawks. This time, however, his argument has drawn a sharp statistical rebuttal from NBA reporter Brett Siegel. Speaking on The Kevin O'Connor Show, Turner made a bold claim about Kuminga's impact after he was traded from Golden State to Atlanta.

"He was their best player from the moment that he showed up in terms of winning impact," Turner said on the Kevin O'Connor show. "He had the best on/off net rating, in the regular season and in the playoffs. In their two wins against the Knicks, who had the best net rating? These are not opinions, these are facts. Who had the best net rating? Jonathan Kuminga."

The clips from the show have become viral on social media, and it reached Siegel's timeline , who offered a much less flattering picture.

"From the time he was traded from the Warriors to the Hawks through the end of the regular season, Jonathan Kuminga ranked 6th on the Hawks in plus-minus. He ranked 5th in total net rating from Feb 24 through the end of the regular season and 9th on the team in the playoffs."

JK ranked sixth on the team in total plus-minus. His +100 mark was well behind Dyson Daniels, who led the Hawks at +300. The sample size matters, too. Jonathan Kuminga only played 16 regular-season games with Atlanta. He missed time after the trade because of injury before returning for the final stretch of the season.

That is hardly enough evidence to label him the team's best player confidently. Also, advanced statistics can tell very different stories when the sample is small.

Kuminga did help Atlanta win two games against the Knicks, and his offense was valuable in those contests. But several of his regular-season games also came late in the year, when some opponents were already focused on the lottery or resting key players. Using that stretch alone to establish Kuminga as Atlanta's best player is unfair to other Hawks stars.

The playoffs made that even clearer. Jonathan Kuminga averaged 13.7 points and 3.3 rebounds during Atlanta's six-game series against New York. He had productive performances in Games 2 and 3, but his overall efficiency remained inconsistent.

His three-point shooting throughout the series showed exactly why there are still questions about his offensive development. He went 0-for-2 from deep in Game 1, 1-for-4 in Game 2, 2-for-4 in Game 3, 0-for-6 in Game 4, and 1-for-5 in Game 5.

Then came Game 6. Kuminga finished with 11 points on 3-of-7 shooting, along with three assists and two rebounds in 23 minutes. The bigger problem was his -44 plus-minus, the worst mark on either team.

The bigger issue is that the discourse is no longer only about Kuminga's basketball ability. Turner has repeatedly found himself defending the decisions surrounding his client's career.

Last year, Turner and Kuminga reportedly turned down a three-year, $75 million structure from Golden State. This summer, Kuminga ultimately agreed to a two-year, roughly $12 million deal with Minnesota, including a player option for the second season.

Turner has argued that the decision was about maintaining flexibility and putting Kuminga in a better position to maximize his next opportunity. All the explanations have not stopped the criticism.

Former NBA player Ty Lawson was among those who reacted strongly , urging Kuminga to part ways with Turner after the interview.

"🤣😂🤣 Johnathan kuminga needs pack his agent up immediately.. send that 'you're fired' letter immediately… There's no way he jumped on camera like this lol."

At 23, Jonathan Kuminga has plenty of time to change and improve his game. Minnesota gives him another opportunity to prove what he can become.

articles.title: Naomi Osaka explains the Allen Iverson influence that plays a role in her career
articles.summary: Tennis star Naomi Osaka discussed the influence that Allen Iverson has had on her career at the 2026 U. S.
articles.body:
Tennis star Naomi Osaka discussed the influence that Allen Iverson has had on her career at the 2026 U.S. Open.

Osaka is one of the most fashion-forward stars in the world of tennis right now, breathing life into the sport's pregame routine with audacious outfits reminiscent of NBA players coming out of the tunnel.

Turns out, that is one of the biggest reasons behind Osaka's dressing style, openly giving the credit to the legendary Allen Iverson for influencing her career.

Naomi Osaka looks up to the trailblazer Allen Iverson

Osaka spoke to the media before her first-round match against Anastasia Zakharova, discussing the impact that Iverson has had on her career by being an athlete involved in fashion.

"For me, he is a trailblazer. He's someone I look up to because he has done a lot in fashion, whether it was on purpose or not… I also think the conversation around clothes in sports and expressing yourself through style; I feel like he is someone I look up to in that regard."

Osaka wore an Allen Iverson-inspired outfit to her pre-tournament press conference, wearing a white sweatshirt with Iverson's image and a throwback 1997 cap for an Iverson-esque fit in 2026.

Iverson is considered to be the figure who truly brought pop culture into the NBA.

Ever since Iverson's rise in the early 2000s, the NBA started setting fashion trends through their biggest superstars rather than just following the lead of the entertainment world.

Iverson made fashion and pop culture synonymous with the NBA, and now Osaka hopes to do the same in the world of tennis.

The much stricter WTA dress code might not allow Osaka the same freedom Iverson had to show off his style, but the 28-year-old American tennis star is maximising the opportunities when she can show off her style.

articles.body:
Oregon is No. 2 in the major polls, it's expected to be knee-deep in the national title hunt, and yes, this really might be the most talented Duck team in the program's history. But Boise State isn't a program that gets fazed by such things. The newest member of the Pac-12 also has big dreams coming into the season as one of the favorites to take the Group of Six spot in the College Football Playoff.

The series history is 3-1, and probably not in the way you would think. Boise State took the first three meetings before Oregon slipped by in a 37-34 fight to start the 2024 season.

Boise State has lost four of its last five season openers after winning six in a row.

Oregon has to travel to Oklahoma State next as it preps for the start of the Big Ten season at USC in late September. Boise State hosts Memphis next week in a huge showdown of Group of Six teams.

Date: Saturday, September 5, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 pm ET TV: CBS Location: Autzen Stadium, Eugene, OR – CFN Week 1 Schedule, Predictions

This is a better Boise State team than last year's version. Quarterback Maddux Madsen is back and healthy, the offensive line is a major plus, and the defensive line has the edge rushers to bring the heat on Oregon quarterback Dante Moore. Oregon's pass rush will be fine, but it wasn't anything special last season and needs to get to Madsen on a regular basis. The Broncos have the potential to control the tempo with short to midrange passes to keep the chains moving. – Boise State 2026 Preview

Can the Boise State defense really hold up against a top offense? Overall, it'll be statistically terrific, but over the last few years it's had a problem producing against the attacks with talent. Washington, Fresno State, Notre Dame, and USF all worked just fine last season against the Broncos, and this Oregon offense should be at a whole other level from those four. But it'll be the other side that should be the bigger problem, with the loaded Duck secondary forcing Madsen to try making the deep plays. Fernando Mendoza was the only quarterback to complete 60% of his passes against Oregon last season. Boise State didn't get to 60% in nine games. – Oregon 2026 Preview

Oregon will come out roaring, and it won't stop. Boise State might have the experience and upside to get tough like it did two years ago in the good three-point loss, but this year's Duck team is stronger. Moore will be razor-sharp from the start, but it'll be the running game that takes over and shows why this is the nation's No. 2 team.

articles.title: Bryson Stott hits a solo HR, Phillies beat the Diamondbacks 2-1 to cap 21-win August
articles.summary: Bryson Stott hit a homer, Aaron Nola provided another solid start on the mound and the Philadelphia Phillies finished a torrid August with a 2-1 victory over...
articles.body:
PHOENIX (AP) — Bryson Stott hit a homer, Aaron Nola provided another solid start on the mound and the Philadelphia Phillies finished a torrid August with a 2-1 victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks on Monday night.

The Phillies have won five straight, 14 of their past 16 and finished with a 21-7 record in August, which was the best mark in the big leagues. They're now just four games behind the Atlanta Braves in the NL East.

Stott crushed a 464-foot homer to right field in the second that gave the Phillies a 1-0 lead. Bryce Harper's double off the center field wall in the third scored Garrett Stubbs and pushed the advantage to 2-0.

Nola (6-10) pitched into the sixth inning, giving up one run on five hits and two walks, striking out five. The veteran right-hander has given up two runs or less in five straight starts.

Alex McFarlane, Orion Kerkering, Brooks Raley, Jose Alvarado and Jhoan Duran combined for four scoreless innings of relief. Duran earned his 29th save in 31 chances, stranding runners on first and third.

Three-time All-Star Ketel Marte made his return for the Diamondbacks , two weeks after he failed to show up for a game in Boston. He was the designated hitter, batted cleanup and was 1 for 3 at the plate with a single and a walk.

The D-backs cut the deficit to 2-1 in the bottom of the third when Geraldo Perdomo scored all the way from first on Gabriel Moreno's double down the left field line.

Arizona is now a half-game behind the San Diego Padres for the third and final NL wild card.

D-backs right-hander Brandon Pfaadt (7-2) gave up two runs on five hits and a walk over six innings, striking out one.

The D-backs send LHP Eduardo Rodriguez (14-4, 2.50 ERA) to the mound on Tuesday night to face Phillies LHP Jesus Luzardo (12-5, 3.09).

articles.title: Stephen Curry Shuts Down Warriors Exit Rumors Amid $136.7 Million Extension Woes; Reconfirms Retirement Plan
articles.summary: Stephen Curry puts an end to all exit speculations by reconfirming his plan to retire with the Warriors.
articles.body:
There has been a lot of speculation about Stephen Curry's future with the Warriors ever since reports claimed their front office is now focusing on the post-Steph era in Golden State. But the 38-year-old Warriors superstar has reassured their fans that he's not going anywhere.

Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry , recently spoke to Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports and clarified that the rumors are not true, but smartly sidestepped why he's delaying the contract extension despite being eligible for a two-year, $136.7 million deal .

"There's no question I want to be here the rest of my career, and I'm pretty sure that's going to happen. The deal and the contract stuff will happen at the right time, and we're not letting it be a distraction from our preparation for the season and the fact that the team we're coming back with has a lot of familiarity."

"Hopefully we can be healthy and just have a chance to show what we're capable of, myself included, missing so many games last year. So, yeah, the goal stays the same. I want to be here. The extension stuff, we'll figure that out at the right time."

"But I'm ready for year 18. It's kind of crazy that it's been this long, and I'm still trying to play at a very high level to help us win, and I'll be able to do my job," Curry concluded .

This should put to rest all the exit rumors that had started popping up ever since the Warriors missed out on the LeBron James sweepstakes . But while Johnson had asked Stephen Curry if he plans to sign this season, saying that he's waiting for 'the right time' only suggests that he's only waiting to be eligible for a three-year extension as a free agent next summer.

Still, there is no certainty on whether Curry will sign that extension deal this summer, as he would become eligible for a contract extension exceeding $200 million in the summer of 2027. But what is certain is that he will stay with the Warriors and does not plan to go anywhere.

The next big question is: how long will Stephen Curry continue playing, now that he turned 38 this year? Johnson asked Ayesha Curry whether her husband, Stephen Curry, has multiple seasons left.

"Of course, Steph is the hardest-working man in the room. He has no days off. He hasn't stopped since last season ended. He's ready. He's ready to get out there. I think we're going to be in for some fun surprises over the next couple of years," she said.

Curry is still playing at a high level but spent most of last season on the bench while suffering from runner's knee. He ended 2025-26 averaging 26.6 points, 4.7 assists, and 3.6 rebounds while shooting 46.8% from the field and 39.3% from behind the three-point line.

So if Stephen Curry is waiting until the summer of 2027 to sign a three-year deal, that means he plans to play until the summer of 2030, when he would have turned 42. But Curry said last season that he is looking at his career in two-year phases, so he may not have planned that far ahead to 2030.

It might turn out he only signs a two-year extension, as he is eligible for. But one thing is certain: his contract extension is now a question of when, not if.

articles.title: Angels end 7-game slide with 10-1 win over sloppy Yankees behind Grissom and Ureña
articles.summary: Vaughn Grissom drove in four runs, rookie Walbert Ureña pitched seven strong innings and the Los Angeles Angels ended a seven-game losing streak with a 10-1...
articles.body:
ANAHEIM, Calif. (AP) — Vaughn Grissom drove in four runs, rookie Walbert Ureña pitched seven strong innings and the Los Angeles Angels ended a seven-game losing streak with a 10-1 victory over the sloppy New York Yankees on Monday night.

Mike Trout had a two-run single and Christian Moore drove in a pair of runs as the Angels won at home for the first time since Aug. 15. Ureña (9-9) gave up five hits with no walks and eight strikeouts.

Elmer Rodríguez (0-3) failed to make it out of the fourth for the Yankees, allowing four runs and four hits with three walks over 3 2/3 innings. It was the shortest of his six career starts since making his major league debut in April.

Spencer Jones homered for the Yankees, who committed three errors after scoring a combined 25 runs in consecutive wins over the rival Boston Red Sox at home last weekend. New York is three games ahead of Boston for the top American League wild card and 4 1/2 games behind first-place Tampa Bay in the AL East.

The Angels took a 1-0 lead in the third on Grissom's run-scoring single. Zach Neto had an RBI single in the fourth after both Oswald Peraza and Tyler Heineman were hit by pitches from Rodríguez with two outs.

Trout added his two-run single in the fourth for his first multi-RBI hit since a two-run homer on July 8.

Jones connected in the fifth to make it 4-1.

Moore had a bloop RBI double in the bottom of the fifth and scored on an errant pickoff throw to second by Michael Fulmer. Neto scored in the sixth for a 7-1 lead when Yankees shortstop José Caballero made two errors on what could have been an inning-ending double-play grounder by Grissom.

In the eighth, Grissom made it 9-1 with a two-run double off the wall in left field and Moore added an RBI single. Grissom finished with three hits and scored twice.

Yankees RHP Gerrit Cole (7-3, 3.19 ERA) faces Angels RHP Grayson Rodriguez (4-5, 6.03) in the middle game of the series Tuesday.

articles.title: Yankees call out Red Sox radio voice for suggesting beaning for late stolen bases
articles.summary: Several New York Yankees are taking exception to comments made by Boston Red Sox radio announcer Will Flemming during a weekend series between the rivals.  J...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Several New York Yankees are taking exception to comments made by Boston Red Sox radio announcer Will Flemming during a weekend series between the rivals.

Jazz Chisholm Jr. was among the players who called out Flemming on Monday after the WEEI radio announcer called the second baseman a "bush league player" for stealing two bases with the Yankees leading 7-1 in the eighth inning of Sunday's series finale .

Chisholm and several teammates also called out Flemming for suggesting Red Sox pitcher Jovani Moran retaliate by beaning Yankees catcher Austin Wells.

"They're called unwritten rules because you're not really breaking any rules," Chisholm told reporters before Monday's game against the Los Angeles Angels. "You've seen teams — actually them — do the same thing where they're pouring on runs. We didn't have nothing to say or nothing to do about it. That's just showing how unprofessional he is."

Flemming apologized on social media for what he said during the telecast.

"Since I have been receiving nonstop calls and threats, I felt like it was important to hop back on here and say: My comments during yesterday's broadcast crossed a line. I'm emotional and a fan at heart and that bled into the broadcast," Flemming posted. "I meant no disrespect to the Yankees players or organization. I could and should have used different words. These rivalry games get me fired up; I apologize for letting the emotion of the moment get the best of me."

articles.title: Commanders get some good news at Monday's practice
articles.summary: Washington was back on the practice field Monday, and so were some key players that were dealing with injuries.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders finalized their initial 53-man roster on Sunday and, on Monday, made two more moves , transferring Laremy Tunsil and Johnny Newton to the injured reserve. After moving Tunsil and Newton to IR with the designation to return, Washington re-signed cornerback Fabian Moreau and defensive tackle Shy Tuttle.

The Commanders returned to practice for the first time since finalizing their roster, and there was some good news. Center Nick Allegretti, quarterback, tight end Ben Sinnott, and defensive tackle Daron Payne were back at practice on Monday.

Allegretti's return is most notable given concerns about the center position. He missed virtually all of training camp after moving over from guard this offseason. Head coach Dan Quinn and general manager Adam Peters are not concerned about Allegretti.

"So, not having Nick for most of camp was something we had to work through, but we have a ton of confidence in him," Peters said. "And he's played, I think 3,000-some-odd snaps in this league. And he's played good football for us before. He went through the whole offseason, so we're really confident. He's not a guy that needs a ton of reps, especially from a mental standpoint."

Allegretti strained his calf on the first day of training camp, which highlighted Washington's depth concerns at center. Those concerns were exacerbated one week later when star left tackle Laremy Tunsil tore his triceps. That move had a domino effect on the line, forcing Brandon Coleman, who was competing to start at left guard, back to left tackle.

Mariota sprained his MCL in the preseason opener, but the prognosis was always that he'd be ready for Week 1. Sinnott was injured late in camp, while Payne was dealing with an undisclosed injury.

Washington opens the season in 13 days on the road at Philadelphia.

articles.title: Driver born with no arms looking to make motorsport history
articles.summary: Callum Smith is set to test his specially-adapted race car at Donnington Park for the first time.
articles.body:
A driver born with no arms says he is determined to make motorsport history by competing at the highest levels - using only his feet.

Callum Smith from Warwickshire learned to drive just two years ago but has now joined Team Brit, a competitive team of disabled racing drivers.

The team has adapted a BMW 1 Series specifically for the driver, who has been passionate about motorsports since childhood.

"My motto in life has always been improvise, adapt and overcome," he said.

His passion was spotted by the all-disabled team which signed him as a rookie driver after a successful test day at Silverstone.

Smith, from Nuneaton, will get his first opportunity to test the adapted car at Donnington Park on 2 September.

The 23-year-old said he had spent his life adapting to everyday challenges.

"I grew up learning to use my feet to do everything," he said.

"I've always believed that if I put my mind to something, I can achieve it.

"Now, fast forward to today, and we're getting ready for my first test in a race car."

Team Brit was established in 2015 and evolved from a charity that provided karting opportunities for disabled armed forces personnel.

Principal Mike Scudamore said it quickly escalated from just one car "back in the day" to four vehicles and eight drivers.

"The most exciting thing about our racing is that there's no class for disability, so we race against able-bodied people all over the UK," Scudamore said.

"Team Brit's ultimate goal is to be the first all-disabled team to race in the world-famous Le Mans 24 hours.

"There have been a couple of disabled drivers that have had a go, but not one team with all their drivers having a disability and we can't wait to try and been the first people to do that."

Smith's race car has been adapted by Coventry company Jim Doran Hand Controls.

They had initially adapted Smith's own car, then were asked if they would consider doing the same for a race car.

Director Dan Doran said: "Callum obviously came to us as a young lad and really didn't really know what adaptions were out there."

Once he was shown the foot steering he knew it was the right thing for him, he said.

For the adapted car "we've basically put the steering wheel on the floor.

"[We've] moved his pedals over a bit and Callum will use his left foot to steer the car and his right foot to operate the brake and accelerator."

"All of us, me and the lads in the workshop, are all excited to help Callum on his journey."

Despite all the adaptations to his car, there are still difficulties for the rookie to overcome before he can become a full-time driver with the team.

To get a licence to compete on the track, Smith will have to prove he can get out of the car unaided in 10 seconds.

But he is determined not to be held back.

"Once I set my mind to something, I'm going to do it," he said.

"This is just another challenge that I'm willing to conquer."

There is also a financial hurdle to overcome - he will need to raise £50,000 to cover the cost of the car conversion, equipment and tuition costs.

So, like many new racing drivers, he is looking for sponsors.

articles.title: Wawrinka feels the love on Grand Slam goodbye
articles.summary: Three-time major champion Stan Wawrinka is given an emotional send-off at the US Open following the final Grand Slam match of his career.
articles.body:
Three-time major champion Stan Wawrinka felt the love at the US Open after being given an emotional send-off following the final Grand Slam match of his career.

The 41-year-old Swiss is retiring at the end of the season and looked close to tears as he received a rapturous reception after a straight-set defeat by Italy's Matteo Berrettini.

Wawrinka, who won the US Open in 2016, was initially overlooked by tournament organisers for a wildcard, but was given a last-minute reprieve following American recipient Patrick Kypson's withdrawal.

The belated decision can be considered well justified given the thousands who packed into the 8,000-capacity Grandstand court at Flushing Meadows.

Wawrinka made heart gestures with his fingers, and put his hand on his heart, at the end of an enjoyable contest to illustrate his appreciation.

With huge cheers already ringing his ears, the former world number three encouraged the crowd to make more noise before knocking balls into the stands as souvenirs of the occasion.

"One of the reasons I played until 41 was to live these moments," said Wawrinka, who also won the Australian Open in 2014 and the French Open in 2015.

"I'm very grateful for this wildcard. It was very important for me to finish here, where I won a Grand Slam 10 years ago. I want to thank you all for all these years."

Wawrinka was only given the news about the wildcard on Wednesday, when he was back in the Swiss mountains having travelled home from New York two days earlier.

Despite the late notice he quickly rearranged a return across the Atlantic in order to play at one of his most loved venues for the final time.

Fans arrived early and waited in long queues to ensure they could witness what they knew could be his Grand Slam goodbye.

It turned out that way as 2021 Wimbledon finalist Berrettini made his veteran opponent pay for not taking his chances.

Wawrinka held set points in each of the first two sets - one in the first and three more in the second - but Berrettini fought them off before running away with the third set.

Berrettini led the applause before Wawrinka addressed the crowd and received a photo montage of his US Open triumph from chief executive Craig Tiley.

Afterwards Wawrinka - celebrated for his one-handed backhand and competitive spirit - said he was "super grateful" for the fond farewell.

"It's showed me that I did the right thing all those 20 years by always trying to fight, always showing up, always trying to do my best, and always trying to push myself to the limits," he added.

"This is what for me was the most important thing - what I get from the fans when I play."

articles.standfirst: Javier Tintó analiza en La Tribu el gran arranque de temporada del brasileño
articles.summary: Javier Tintó analiza en La Tribu el gran arranque de temporada del brasileño
articles.body: Javier Tintó, María José Hostalrich, Ricardo Rosety, Yon Cuezva y Pipi Estrada han sido los tertulianos de este martes en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, para analizar la victoria del Barça, con dobletes de Lamine Yamal y Raphinha, y la retirada de Leo Messi de la selección argentina. Javier Tintó. "Raphinha es un buen ejemplo de la tomadura de pelo de la temporada pasada de jugadores que se prepararon para el Mundial, pasaron de los clubes y ahora están como motos, tipo Bellingham o Mbappé. Raphinha me parece el jugador referencia del Barça, más que Lamine, y eso que el Barça le quiso vender este verano. Es un jugador que siempre ha sido un poco maltratado por el Barça. Me parece el líder del equipo". María José Hostalrich. "El Barcelona tiene un montón de recursos para hacer lo que le dé la gana, para jugar como quiera, tiene dobladas las posiciones". Ricardo Rosety. "Cada verano hay mucho runrún con Raphinha. Le cambia la cara Nico Williams, la amenaza de que Nico llegue al Barcelona cambia la actitud y el rendimiento del brasileño. El éxito de la temporada del Barça depende de que Flick consiga mantener este nivel de intensidad, trabajo y sacrificio. Si es así, el resto de equipos no tienen nada que hacer". articles.title: 'Barba Gris', el aventurero de 91 años que firma un récord de 3.530 km en los Apalaches
articles.standfirst: Dale Sanders, el senderista de mayor edad en completar esta travesía, ha tardado casi un año, en el que ha sufrido más de 70 caídas, alguna de las cuales necesitó hasta hospitalización
articles.summary: Dale Sanders, el senderista de mayor edad en completar esta travesía, ha tardado casi un año, en el que ha sufrido más de 70 caídas, alguna de las cuales necesitó hasta hospitalización
articles.body: Ni las 71 caídas que sufrió en un año, alguna de las cuales requirió hospitalización, apartaron a Dale Sanders, más conocido como 'Barba Gris', del desafío de recuperar su récord de erigirse en el excursionista de mayor edad en completar el Sendero de los Apalaches. A sus 91 años, 'Barba Gris' completó los 3.530 kilómetros de este sendero, que conecta Springer Mountain en Georgia con el Monte Katahdin en Maine, en menos de 12 meses, el tiempo que la Appalachian Trail Conservancy (el organismo que certifica y registra de forma oficial estos registros) establece para recorrer todos los tramos del sendero en cualquier orden, incluyendo también las pausas. “Tuve que darle las gracias a Dios, a mi equipo de apoyo y a todos los que me ayudaron a llegar hasta aquí”, dijo el excursionista, que sufrió distintos percances durante la aventura. Entre ellas protagonizó numerosos tropiezos, que acabaron con lesiones y rozaduras en las piernas, los brazos y las manos. “Gracias a Dios no me rompí nada, pero me di unos golpes”, dijo. “No me froté para quitarme la sangre, simplemente seguí caminando”. Semanas después de una de las caídas en el descanso del monte Killington, a 'Barba Gris' se le entumeció el brazo izquierdo y acabó en un hospital de Maine. Lo que los médicos temían inicialmente que fuera un derrame cerebral resultó ser un nervio pinzado. Aunque pronto le dieron el alta para volver a practicar senderismo, ahí Dale Sanders consideró la posibilidad de abandonar el reto. Sin embargo, tras pasar por su domicilio, su esposa lo animó a continuar. Eso le ha convertido en casi una estrella entre otros excursionistas. Miles de personas le siguen en redes y han visto de cerca su desafío. 'Barba Gris', antiguo Marine, acumula diversos récords relacionados con la edad, entre ellos el de ser la persona de mayor edad en recorrer en kayak el río Mississippi, un viaje de 87 días que comenzó el día de su 87 cumpleaños. Cuando era niño, sufrió acoso escolar por su baja estatura, pero pudo superarlo gracias a deportes como la acrobacia y la natación. 'Barba Gris' recuperó así un récord de edad para recorrer el Sendero de los Apalaches que había establecido por primera vez en 2017, a los 82 años, y lo mantuvo durante cuatro años. Después, lo batió MJ 'Nimblewill Nomad' Eberhart en 2021, a los 83 años.

articles.title: Penta Primed for an All-Timer vs. Roman Reigns, Rey Fénix Shines in Defeat, More WWE Raw Fallout
articles.summary: The Rocket Arena in Cleveland, Ohio hosted the August 31 episode of Raw on Netflix where Penta and Rey Fénix stole the show and the stable warfare continued.
articles.body:
The Rocket Arena in Cleveland hosted the August 31 episode of WWE Raw on Netflix where Penta and Rey Fénix stole the show and the stable warfare continued.

Penta defeated his brother to earn the next World Heavyweight Championship opportunity against Roman Reigns.

Royce Keys and OTM attacked The Usos, forcing Jacob Fatu to declare war against his former friend. Reigns again dealt with LA Knight, who taunted the champion.

Who shined? Who struggled? Where does WWE go from here? Check out all the fallout from Raw below.

Roman Reigns vs. Penta Will Be WWE TV Match of the Year

Is Penta the best WWE in-ring worker of 2026? He has certainly made a compelling case.

Time and again, when WWE has let the unique luchador perform, he has delivered beyond usual expectations.

His match with Rey Fénix was always going to be great, but for a fresh WWE audience, this was one of the best TV matches of the year.

The two brothers were unstoppable in the ring, running and flying at a confident pace that few could match.

That said, Penta's best match of the year is still to come. He has earned a chance to face Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship.

There is no chance Penta actually wins, but the excitement building for this match is the potential of these two unique stars colliding for the first time.

Reigns has not faced anyone quite like Penta in many years. His hard-hitting style matched with his lucha libre speed will make him a unique threat to The OTC.

If they get time in Mexico City, Reigns will be pushed to deliver the best work of his career in years to keep up with Penta's unreal pace.

That is a recipe for success, a match that could be talked about for years to come.

Rey Fénix Has Earned Much Bigger Spotlight

While Penta delivered another expected impressive performance on Raw, WWE fans are still somewhat unfamiliar with Rey Fénix.

That made his work with Penta all the more memorable. The two men went out of their way to sell that they are relative equals in the ring.

There is no better time to push Fénix, who has finally started to show the potential he showcased much more regularly before he signed with WWE.

This is a former AAA Mega champion and AEW international champion who can deliver at the highest level in the ring.

He could be a memorable challenger in the United States Championship scene on SmackDown immediately.

In the long term, Fénix should be a champion in WWE, not just AAA, because his talent will elevate anyone who challenges him for the gold.

Jacob Fatu Ready to Turn on Roman Reigns

The spirit of Jacob Fatu has been overshadowed by Roman Reigns, but he has not been forgotten.

The Samoan Werewolf is an untapped Superstar who could genuinely take over WWE with the right opportunity.

If Fatu can just break away from The Bloodline, he can become a dangerous threat in the company as a whole, one of the top heels in the business.

That villainous turn could be on the horizon based on small teases on Raw.

In particular, the way Fatu has moved when it comes to Solo Sikoa and LA Knight vs. Royce Keys and OTM.

While The Samoan Werewolf verbally declared war against Keys and OTM, he physically attacked and bloodied Sikoa.

Fatu could easily be playing The Bloodline while working with former friend Keys. And if The Samoan Werewolf is behind Keys and OTM, he suddenly becomes Raw's top heel.

That is a massive spotlight that could quickly change the landscape of Monday nights.

Why Doesn't Raw Have More Women's Stars?

Raquel Rodriguez received some help from Lyra Valkyria in defending her Women's Intercontinental Championship against Sol Ruca, but it was still a big win for the titleholder.

At the moment, there is little point in running additional matches between Raquel and Ruca as the champion needs to move on to fresh competition.

The problem is that no one is stepping up to challenge Big Mami Cool besides Ruca. There is no clear next woman up for the Women's Intercontinental Championship.

This is a problem because it limits the champion and her potential to define herself beyond Liv Morgan and The Judgment Day.

This is Raquel's first singles title run on Raw. Her career could be defined by her reign, yet that run is starting slow and looking to slow down even more.

Instead of waiting for Ruca and Valkyria to feud, WWE should send over fresh names for Raquel, even if they are underused talents on SmackDown such as Jordynne Grace or Giulia.

NXT has multiple stars who could use a trial run on Raw like Kendal Grey, Jaida Parker or Wren Sinclair.

It is time to take some chances and see who could add depth to a Raw women's division that lacks depth.

Joe Hendry has frequently disappeared from Raw since his initial debut earlier in the year, and each time he returns, it feels like WWE cares less about him.

Coming in to help Je'Von Evans against Dominik Mysterio and JD McDonagh just to lose is not the role he would have played a few months ago.

With Logan Paul's injury, his first feud was delayed, but it feels much more like WWE has lost faith in his star power.

This may have been influenced by the horrendous Danhausen concert segment, but Danhausen has stayed in mostly the same position since then.

More likely, Hendry has just done little to shine in the same way he did in sporadic appearances for WWE before.

The biggest culprit for this decline is a lack of creativity. The Scot was constantly used in creative ways in NXT whenever he appeared, but on Raw, he is just another body.

His matches are forgettable, and his big chances to deliver concerts or surprise appearances have lacked the joyful flair he once possessed before signing with WWE.

There may not be an easy answer for Hendry, but he needs to find some way to convince WWE to go a bit more wild with him again sooner rather than later.

The concerts are fine, but the heart of his gimmick was his sudden, fiery arrivals to help other faces that always turned the tide.

Hendry needs to be treated like a real problem when he appears. Otherwise, there is no point to saying his name.

articles.title: NHL Trade Targets Big Board for September 2026
articles.summary: The calendar has flipped to September, and not a moment too soon for NHL fans enduring a mostly quiet summer in the trade market.
articles.body:
The calendar has flipped to September, and not a moment too soon for NHL fans enduring a mostly quiet summer in the trade market.

Following a flurry of activity involving NHL players from June 16 to July 2, only five trades have occurred since , all involving minor leaguers.

That means that our NHL Trade Targets Big Board for this month contains many of the players featured in our August 2026 rankings .

That includes such notable stars as Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck, Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin, and Vancouver Canucks winger Brock Boeser. They continued to feature prominently in media trade speculation throughout August.

Some new names join this month's list. They include Anaheim Ducks winger Chris Kreider and Calgary Flames defenseman Zach Whitecloud.

Several players from our previous list have dropped to an honorable mention listing. That doesn't mean they won't be trade candidates, only that things were so quiet throughout August that they weren't mentioned in most media trade chatter. We believe they're still worth monitoring as trade chips.

Follow along to see where these players end up in our September Trade Targets Big Board. As always, we based it on the player's skill, experience, contract, and most importantly, the possibility of being traded.

Marchenko was ranked No. 2 on our August Trade Targets Big Board after rumors linked him to the Montreal Canadiens. There's been no further speculation about the 25-year-old scoring winger, but that doesn't mean he won't resurface as a trade candidate.

Wright sat at No. 3 on our August list following reports claiming the Kraken were willing to move him in a package deal for a scorer. The buzz around the 22-year-old center faded through August, but it'll be interesting to see if he pops up in trade rumors as training camp approaches.

The No. 3 player on our previous Trade Targets ranking, Nikishin is a restricted free agent still awaiting a new contract with the Hurricanes. In June, it was reported that they were mulling over whether to trade or sign the 24-year-old defenseman. The rumors died throughout August but could resume before training camp.

Schneider was No. 7 on our previous list. He avoided salary arbitration with the Rangers by agreeing to a one-year, $5.5 million contract in July, but the short term of that deal raised questions about the 25-year-old defenseman's future in New York. With training camp on the horizon, those questions could persist.

Bryan Rust and Rickard Rakell, Pittsburgh Penguins

Rust and Rakell were 9 and 8 respectively on our previous list. They frequently surfaced in the rumor mill over the past two summers, so it was unsurprising they popped up again. We can't rule out the retooling Penguins doing more roster tinkering that involves one or both veteran forwards.

The 25-year-old Blue Jackets center surfaced in the rumor mill in July as a potential trade target for the New York Rangers or Montreal Canadiens. We had him at No. 12 on our previous list. Since then, there's been no indication he's on the trade block, but we can't dismiss that possibility.

An unrestricted free agent next summer, DeBrincat sat at No. 13 on our previous list. Uncertainty over the Red Wings' direction as they search for a new general manager raised questions about his future in Detroit. However, nothing will happen until the Wings hire a new GM.

The No. 15 player on our previous NHL Trade Targets Board , Elias Pettersson's future with the Vancouver Canucks remains the subject of offseason media conjecture.

During an appearance on the Canucks Conversation podcast , CHEK-TV's Rick Dhaliwal dismissed speculation linking Pettersson to the Los Angeles Kings. Pettersson was spotted training in Los Angeles earlier this summer, but Dhaliwal noted his wife is from there and he usually spends part of his time training there.

Dhaliwal also said that a trade involving Pettersson hasn't been close to happening for several months. He claimed that teams were checking in, but nothing reached the point where the Canucks would approach the 27-year-old center and his agent about waiving his no-movement clause .

Pettersson's expensive contract and his declining production are the main reasons why he's likely to remain with the Canucks this season. It would take a significant change for a deal to take place, like the Canucks agreeing to retain half of his $11.6 million annual cap hit.

It wouldn't be an NHL offseason without Erik Karlsson popping up in the rumor mill. The 36-year-old Pittsburgh Penguins defenseman sat at No. 14 on our previous Trade Targets board amid speculation he might be traded to the Toronto Maple Leafs or Ottawa Senators before the regular season begins.

Karlsson is slated to become an unrestricted free agent next summer. Given his age, the Penguins are unlikely to re-sign him, but they could retain him for this season as they attempt to build on last season's promising performance.

During the Aug. 25 episode of 32 Thoughts: The Podcast , Elliotte Friedman said one of his sources predicted that Karlsson could be traded to the Maple Leafs, depending on how this season unfolded for both clubs.

Karlsson has full control over his situation this season with a full no-movement clause , and there's no certainty he'd want to go to Toronto if he became available. Still, his situation could be worth monitoring in the coming weeks, especially if the Penguins get off to a poor start.

Speculation over whether the Minnesota Wild would re-sign or trade Quinn Hughes landed the 26-year-old superstar defenseman at No. 13 on our June 1 NHL Trade Block Big Board . However, the trade rumors faded as the Wild and the Hughes camp held contract extension talks.

So far, there's no indication that Hughes and the Wild are close to an extension. He carries a $7.9 million cap hit on his current contract and can become an unrestricted free agent next July. He will more than double his salary on his next deal, perhaps rising to $20 million per season.

Hughes' desire to play one day with his brothers Jack and Luke prompted James Nichols of New Jersey Hockey Now to speculate about what it might cost the Devils to acquire him from the Wild if contract talks fall through. He also noted that Wild GM Bill Guerin is preaching patience regarding their negotiations.

On Aug. 25, Wild beat writer Michael Russo of The Athletic reported the negotiations were ongoing. He also cited sources dismissing internet rumors claiming the Wild and Devils were in trade talks regarding Hughes. Nevertheless, the longer Hughes remains unsigned, the more speculation about his future.

Eligible for unrestricted free-agent status next July, Pavel Zacha sat at No. 6 on our August Trade Targets Big Board . Speculation over the 29-year-old center's future with the Boston Bruins remains as training camp approaches.

Zacha had a career-best 30 goals and 65 points last season. He's entering the final season of a four-year contract with a $4.8 million salary-cap hit and will seek a substantial raise on his next deal.

On Aug. 10, Steve Conroy of the Boston Herald included Zacha's contract status among his lingering offseason questions he felt the Bruins must address. He believes the veteran forward's durability and reliability make him worth retaining, but acknowledged that his trade value is at its peak.

We noted on our previous boards that the Bruins hope to re-sign Zacha, but they were also open to trade offers. Given the current silence on the matter, they could retain him for this season as contract talks continue, but we can't rule out a trade.

Sitting at No. 11 on our previous NHL Trade Targets board , Brock Boeser has been a frequent subject of trade speculation over the past two seasons. It's no surprise the 29-year-old winger has resurfaced in the rumor mill.

On Aug. 25, TSN's Travis Yost suggested Boeser could become a trade candidate as the Canucks continue to rebuild their roster. He noted the veteran winger's declining production since his career-best 40-goal, 73-point performance in 2023-24 and acknowledged his best years could be behind him.

Nevertheless, Yost believes that Boeser is a better player than his recent stats suggest. His production could improve playing on a deeper club with better linemates.

Boeser is in the second season of a seven-year contract with an average annual value of $7.5 million. He also has a full no-movement clause. So far, there's no indication that he's available in the trade market, but his situation could be worth watching if the Canucks become sellers again this season.

The Calgary Flames acquired Morgan Frost from the Philadelphia Flyers in a multi-player trade in January 2025. With the 27-year-old center eligible to become an unrestricted free agent next July, he's surfaced in offseason conjecture as a trade candidate.

Frost is in the final season of a two-year contract with an affordable average annual value of $4.4 million and an eight-team no-trade list. He could become a prime trade chip for the Flames if they're sellers again by the March 1 trade deadline, especially given the value placed on centers by NHL clubs.

On Aug. 18, Kent Wilson of the Calgary Sun included Frost among his list of players the Flames could peddle this season. He's never reached the 50-point plateau in his seven NHL seasons, but had a career-best 22 goals and 43 points with the depleted Flames in 2025-26.

Wilson believes that a strong showing by Frost could make him an attractive trade target. He might not be moved in an early-season deal, but his performance in 2026-27 and his UFA eligibility next summer will make him a player worth watching.

On July 1, 2025, the Montréal Canadiens acquired Zachary Bolduc from the St. Louis Blues. Over a year later, conjecture suggests the 23-year-old winger could be on the move again as he awaits a new contract with the Canadiens.

Bolduc is a restricted free agent coming off his entry-level contract. Stu Cowan of The Montreal Gazette suggested on Aug. 12 that Bolduc and teammate Arber Xhekaj could be "sign-and-trade" candidates, perhaps to acquire a top-six forward.

After a promising 19-goal, 36-point rookie campaign with the Blues in 2024-25, Bolduc struggled in his first season with the Canadiens. He bounced around the roster, finishing with 12 goals and 30 points. However, Bolduc showed some grit in the postseason while netting seven points in 19 games.

Cowan believes there would be teams interested in Bolduc and Xhekaj if they become available. While there's no sign yet that either player will be moved, Bolduc's contract status continues to raise questions about his immediate future.

The Calgary Flames spent the past two seasons rebuilding their roster by trading veterans for draft picks, prospects, and young players. If that trend continues, Zach Whitecloud could feature prominently in this season's rumor mill.

Whitecloud was acquired from the Vegas Golden Knights in last January's Rasmus Andersson trade . The 29-year-old defenseman fit in quickly on the Flames' blue line. With eight NHL seasons under his belt and a Stanley Cup on his resume, he's their most experienced rearguard.

On Aug. 10, Kent Wilson of the Calgary Sun observed that Whitecloud remained in last season's rumor mill despite his acquisition by the Flames. He believed that the blueliner's experience, versatility, and affordable contract could make him their most valuable trade chip .

Whitecloud is signed through 2027-28 with an average annual value of $2.8 million and lacks no-trade protection. The Flames could keep him around to mentor their young defensemen, but he could be worth monitoring as a trade candidate this season.

The 2025-26 season wasn't one that Los Angeles Kings goaltender Darcy Kuemper will remember fondly. His inconsistent play cost him the starter's job to Anton Forsberg, making him the subject of trade rumors that landed him on our two NHL Trade Block Big Boards in June.

Kuemper, 35, is in the final season of his five-year contract with a salary-cap hit of $5.3 million and a 10-team no-trade list. That would make him an expensive backup if he cannot regain the starting goalie role from Forsberg for this season.

On Aug. 13, Ryan O'Hara of The Hockey News took note of the uncertainty regarding Kuemper's future with the Kings, especially with Peter Laviolette coming in as their new head coach. O'Hara points out that Laviolette prefers a clear-cut starting goalie.

O'Hara believes teams could be in the market for an experienced starter like Kuemper, noting that he was a Vezina Trophy finalist in 2024-25. Perhaps one of those clubs might take a chance on Kuemper, especially if injuries occur during training camp and preseason.

The Anaheim Ducks' salary-cap payroll for 2026-27 took an unexpected hit on July 3, when the Philadelphia Flyers signed center Leo Carlsson to a five-year offer sheet with an average annual value of $18 million. The Ducks matched the offer on July 9, leaving them with $9.03 million in cap space .

That has complicated the Ducks' efforts to re-sign winger Cutter Gauthier, who led the club with 41 goals and 69 points last season. Given the hefty raise Carlsson received, the 21-year-old Gauthier has set a high price for his next contract. He reportedly rejected a four-year offer worth $13 million AAV.

The Ducks must at some point shed salary to sign Gauthier, which could make Alex Killorn a trade candidate. The Hockey News ' Andre Leal suggested the 36-year-old winger, who is in the final year of a four-year contract with an AAV of $6.3 million.

Killorn's age, declining performance, and 15-team no-trade list could make him difficult to move. Nevertheless, his playoff experience and defensive skills could make him enticing for a club seeking that type of forward.

On Aug. 13, Ryan O'Hara of The Hockey News suggested that the Los Angeles Kings could gear up for another roster shakeup this season. He believes that winger Trevor Moore could benefit from a change of scenery.

Moore, 31, is signed through 2027-28 , with an average annual value of $4.2 million and lacking no-trade protection. He had a career-best 31 goals and 57 points in 2023-24, but injuries and inconsistency sent his production tumbling to 40 points in 71 games in 2024-25 and 32 points in 69 games last season.

O'Hara praised Moore's speed and ability but pointed out that he hasn't consistently secured a top-six role with the Kings. Nevertheless, he believes the winger could attract some interest in the trade market.

It could take some time before the Kings make any significant roster changes this season. However, a club in the market for an experienced middle-six forward with an affordable contract might make a pitch for Moore at some point this season.

As training camp approaches, Arber Xhekaj still awaits a new contract. The 25-year-old Montréal Canadiens defenseman is a restricted free agent coming off a two-year deal with an affordable average annual value of $1.3 million.

The 6'4", 240-pound Xhekaj is popular among his teammates and Canadiens fans for his physical style of play. However, his limited ice time last season and the presence of promising young defensemen like David Reinbacher and Adam Enstrom made him the subject of trade conjecture.

Xhekaj was at No. 10 on our previous Trade Targets Board . On Aug. 12, Stu Cowan of The Montreal Gazette speculated that the big blueliner (and winger Zachary Bolduc) could be "sign-and-trade" candidates, perhaps in a package deal for a top-six forward.

So far, there's no indication the Canadiens intend to peddle Xhekaj on his own or with another player. However, the longer he remains unsigned, the more speculation grows about his future in Montréal.

The Anaheim Ducks acquired Chris Kreider from the New York Rangers in June 2025. However, the 35-year-old left winger could be on the move again if the Ducks make cost-cutting trades to free up salary cap space to re-sign leading scorer Cutter Gauthier.

Matching a five-year offer sheet from the Philadelphia Flyers for Leo Carlsson worth an AAV of $18 million left the Ducks with $9.03 million in cap space for this season . Soon afterward, the 21-year-old Gauthier reportedly rejected a four-year offer worth $13 million.

Kreider is in the final year of his contract with an AAV of $6.5 million and will become an unrestricted free agent next summer. Andre Leal of The Hockey News included the veteran winger among his list of players the Ducks could peddle to clear sufficient cap space to re-sign Gauthier.

Moving Kreider won't be easy because of his age and his 15-team no-trade list. However, his 22-goal, 50-point performance last season showed he still has the scoring punch to entice another club in need of an experienced middle-six forward.

It's been three months since Dylan Larkin's trade request was first reported. Since then, the 30-year-old Detroit Red Wings center has been a fixture in the NHL rumor mill and on our NHL Trade Targets Boards, sitting at No. 5 in our August edition .

However, Larkin's request remains in limbo as the Red Wings continue to search for a new general manager. Assistant GM Shawn Horcoff currently handles day-to-day management duties, but that doesn't extend to trades .

According to Bob Duff of Detroit Hockey Now, don't expect Larkin to stage a holdout from training camp or the start of the season to force the issue. That would put him at risk of breaching his contract , giving the Red Wings justification to suspend him without pay.

Larkin has little choice but to wait until the new general manager is hired. He'll likely meet with the new GM soon afterward to determine his future. Until we hear differently, he remains among our notable trade targets.

For the past two months, Connor Hellebuyck sat atop our NHL Trade Targets Big Board .

We considered the 33-year-old Winnipeg Jets goaltender to be the player most likely to be moved after weeks of intense trade speculation, including reports of a rumored deal with the Buffalo Sabres that fell through.

Hellebuyck is signed through 2030-31 with an $8.5 million AAV and a full no-movement clause. He revealed his trade request on Aug. 27, but whether that spurs the Jets to move him before the season begins remains to be seen. Nevertheless, it secures his spot on top of this month's trade targets board.

Jets beat writer Murat Ates of The Athletic believes the club's asking price is a top-six forward (preferably a center or right wing) and a goalie who can help to ease Hellebuyck's departure. He listed the Carolina Hurricanes, Florida Panthers, Vegas Golden Knights, New Jersey Devils and Buffalo Sabres as destinations.

The Sabres also appear on Joe Yerdon's destination list for Hellebuyck. That's because the two clubs were working on a deal that would've sent the three-time Vezina Trophy winner to Buffalo in June, but the deal fell through. Time will tell if they revisit those discussions.

Stats via NHL.com . Salary and contract info via PuckPedia .

INMAN, Kan. (KSNW) — The Inman Teutons are coming off an 8-2 season with senior quarterback Malachi Brunk at the center of the offense.

Brunk is a four-year starter for Inman and was just short of 2,500 all-purpose yards last season. The senior quarterback threw for 18 touchdowns last season, many to his top target, Korbyn McLellan, who also returns this year.

There is no doubting the senior class has plenty of experience — not just from playing the game, but from playing together.

"This class and the class under us, we've played football since like preschool together. And our goal has always been to win the state championship. So that's our goal for this year," Brunk said.

Inman head coach Lance Sawyer believes his players know exactly what they want to accomplish this season.

"I think our kids know where they want to be. They want to end up in Hutch by the end of this year," Sawyer said. "And we got a long ways to go, and we got to stay healthy to do it. But we're excited for it."

Inman will make the trip to take on Sedgwick this Friday at 7 p.m.

Well, he once sat upon a golden throne. Literally. Check the recruiting photos.

Moore was committed to Notre Dame — the betting co-favorite alongside Ohio State to capture college football's national title this season — during his high school recruitment. He ultimately signed with UCLA before transferring to Oregon.

Manning's Texas Longhorns , Carr's Fighting Irish and Moore's Ducks all are consensus Top 5 teams, with Oregon (2), Texas (4) and Notre Dame (5) bunched together in the US LBM Coaches Poll .

Moore is a past participant in the famed Manning Passing Academy ; Arch Manning and Carr participated this year.

USA TODAY Sports spoke with a head coach of a camp participant and a quarterback at the camp to get the early skinny on the Carr-Manning debate.

"Both guys were great," the quarterback said. "Super talented. But, I had some classroom stuff with Carr. Unbelievable dude. Throwing the football? I'm taking Carr every day of the week."

There's much more to playing QB than throwing the football, but Carr, whose stock continues to surge following his work at the Manning Passing Academy , continues to elevate.

"When my guy got back," the head coach said, "he told me CJ was the best quarterback there that week."

How does the NFL, in part, view the potential of the 2027 NFL Draft class at the quarterback position?

"I think the class can be elite," an NFC scout told USA TODAY Sports. "Don't sleep on (Drew) Mestemaker at Oklahoma State! I think he's a dude.

"(The class is) Significantly better than '26."

No one is advocating the firing of anyone. Let's be clear.

Let's also be clear: A lot of college football coaches are going to get fired this fall into the winter.

There's a national championship-winning coach itching for his return, a number of active coaches and other figures in the college athletics landscape told USA TODAY Sports.

Jimbo Fisher, after working to be in the mix this past coaching cycle at Auburn specifically, is ready for a return to the sideline.

Multiple coaches and agents informed USA TODAY Sports of Fisher's desire to return to the game, noting money (coaching salary) would not be a prohibitive factor for a coach looking to again prove himself.

Fisher, working with the ACC Network, also spent time earlier this year with new Memphis coach Charles Huff, among other stops in the past two years since his departure from Texas A&M.

This is Fisher's third year off the sidelines following his dismissal from Texas A&M late in the 2023 season.

On the heels of a recent practice, the Wolverines were commanded to run "gassers" near the end of the preseason camp.

Kyle Whittingham's message, USA TODAY Sports was told, was simple.

"We will NOT be soft," the coach intoned.

Additionally, as Michigan adopts to a more evolved, forward-thinking front-office model, we're told the Wolverines' personnel staff have been ushered through 'Scout School,' with NFL personnel reaching out to help provide guidance on evaluative techniques as well as other elements of the player-identification process.

Ranking the top 25 party schools in the US. Who does it best?

How nuanced are the contracts of current college football players, especially as it pertains to potential guaranteed monies, incentives and … delicately worded language?

Consider this example an NIL agent shared about a direct situation he encountered with a client in the most recent portal (read: transactional) cycle:

"We were in talks with (ACC school) and we were talking about starts," the agent said." He had started every game the year before at his previous school, but he was coming off injury.

"So, they said, 'We wouldn't say he's the starter in the contract, but it was something to the effect of the work-around feature as what if we say he's a starter in pre-game lineup introductions? Like, the starting lineup announcements on the video board in pre-game."

"We agreed to exactly that," the agent said.

The result? A contract worth more than $400,000.

Longest Yard, Part II: Meet Kamden Sixkiller

All those best-name team accolades in college football, and somehow Kamden Sixkiller 's flying under the radar.

Quarterback of the Campbell Camels FCS squad (Roll Humps is their enduring motto), Sixkiller also is his conference's player of the week after accounting for 438 yards' total offense in Campbell's 49-37, not-that-close upset-win on the road at Southern Conference preseason contender ETSU. The Bucs are helmed by former Charlotte coach Will Healy.

The Camels, entering Year 3 under Braxton Harris, turned loose Sixkiller in the Week 0 opener. All he did? Deliver 343 passing yards and four total touchdowns.

Is that Sixkiller name sticking in the cobwebs? It probably should.

Kamden Sixkiller is a relative of Sonny Sixkiller, a former star quarterback at Washington who also starred in the original Hollywood gridiron classic, "The Longest Yard."

"He played against me when he was a true freshman at McNeese," Harris told USA TODAY Sports, confirming the younger Sixkiller's connection to the 1970s star. "I thought he was a stud, and when the coaching change happened, I jumped all over him."

In its first year as an Football Championship Subdivision program, West Florida has just crashed the national rankings on the heels of an opening win — even if it faces the expected multiple years of transitional status, per NCAA guidelines.

The program's coach, Kaleb Nobles, was part of West Florida's first football team after beginning his college career at Valdosta State. His wife, Katy, is a former West Florida volleyball player.

All his team did in its inaugural game as an FCS program was build double-digit leads of 27-9 and 34-24 before holding on to win against Southern Illinois, which won seven of 11 games last season against FCS foes and has been a regular playoff contender.

In addition to his playing career, Nobles' resume includes work under Dabo Swinney and Tony Elliott at Clemson.

Who has the best helmet in college football? We rank the top 25

Concord University, in Athens, W.V., just scored that program's first win against an FCS opponent by going on the road to record a season-opening 41-35 victory at Davidson.

Under second-year coach Cody Edwards, Concord utilized a 10-0 third quarter to permanently dislodge a tied contest.

Among the former coaches for whom Edwards has worked are ex-NFL head and assistant coaches Brandon Staley and Tom Arth.

Additionally, Edwards has hired well. His offensive coordinator, Benton Duby, has notable Power conference experience prior to his arrival at the tiny West Virginia school.

Duby's stops include Mississippi State, Oklahoma and Ole Miss. In this game, his offense merely worked host Davidson for more than 460 yards' offense despite just 23-plus minutes of possession.

articles.title: What does C.J. Okoye bring to the NY Giants? Looking at the good, and the bad
articles.summary: The New York Giants traded a seventh-round pick for C.J. Okoye, who provides important defensive line depth.
articles.body:
The New York Giants traded a 2028 seventh-round pick to the Baltimore Ravens for C.J. Okoye . The 6-foot-6, 365-pound defensive lineman was part of the International Pathway Program and spent much of the 2025 season on the Ravens' active roster, where he played 214 snaps for John Harbaugh.

New York had interest and ensured that Okoye was a New York Giant prior to final cuts. As expected, Okoye was on the Giants' 53-man roster. Here are some highlights of Okoye from the preseason:

C.J. Okoye wears No. 97 and 91 in the plays below

A few things are evident on tape. For starters, he's massive. Some outlets have him listed at 370 pounds. He has long 33¾-inch arms and just under 10-inch hands.

Okoye has some serious push at the point of attack, and he generates good force into his bull-rush. His rush repertoire is based on the bull-rush to push the pocket, which is his primary move, but he does a good job getting his eyes on the quarterback and adjusting mid-play. There's no doubting his strength, especially when he keeps his hips and pads low.

The combination he landed against Washington was mpressive for Okoye, who is still a young player learning the position. He landed a hump-move and transitioned it into a club swim against a reaching guard off the play-action. The pass was somehow completed, but the rush showed a finesse game that — if mastered — would make Okoye a dangerous threat on the defensive line.

Here's a play from the regular season where Okoye drew a holding penalty based on the aforementioned push and lower-body drive that he possesses. He's also solid with his vision and awareness; he keeps his eyes open when rushing to cut angles off against mobile quarterbacks who try to escape the pocket.

Okoye showed exceptional awareness by pushing the pocket and closing throwing lanes with his long wingspan. His eyes are an underrated trait, especially for a player who is relatively new to football.

Okoye displayed a solid anchor against one-on-one blocks last year. Above, we watch him use his awareness and vision to locate Chase Brown (30) in the hole. The B-Gap opened up, and Okoye was able to close it from the A, while hand fighting the center.

Okoye gets a good jump off the snap and catches, neutralizing the center's blocking attempt, forcing the football to bounce inside and into a waiting defender. Okoye has solid regular-season reps on a talented team, and he'll fit into the Giants rotation well.

Okoye is a massive man who plays high at times, allowing blockers to control/steer him too frequently. When he plays low, though, he's difficult to move. But that high nature can be a liability. The zone looks, specifically, where Okoye gets his feet moving laterally, have led to blocks where he gets displaced due to his high nature. It happened a few times versus the Bengals last season:

Okoye can field double teams and anchor, but he was displaced a few times on tape due to the pad-level issue.

Planet theory — the Giants traded for a massive human being with potential and familiarity to their coaching staff. When precise with his technique and pad level, Okoye is almost immovable in one-on-one blocks, with a solid ability to anchor in the ground, but staying low is an issue for the 6-6 defensive lineman. Still, he's a high-processing player with excellent push into contact, and he's flashed adroit hand usage and has strung some moves together, albeit I wouldn't count on him being a pass-rushing specialist.

Okoye will be a rotational defensive lineman for the Giants; one who will battle for snaps with Bobby Jameson-Travis and Darius Alexander. It's not out of the realm of possibility that Okoye earns the number three defensive tackle role behind veterans D.J. Reader and Shelby Harris ( not including Chauncey Golston) . It was a good trade to get Harbaugh a familiar player at a position of need. Okoye is still only 24years old.

1. FC Union Berlin have confirmed the arrival of Swiss midfielder Kastriot Imeri from BSC Young Boys.

"Now I'm looking forward to bringing my skills to the team, getting to know the squad and experiencing many special moments together with our fans."

Union director of men's professional football Horst Heldt is delighted with the arrival of the versatile midfielder, who can operate both out wide and in a central attacking role.

"Kastriot is a technically gifted and versatile attacking player who can be deployed both between the lines and out wide. He is very well-trained, brings experience from top-flight Swiss football and international competition, and has already demonstrated his potential at the highest level on numerous occasions," Heldt said.

"We are convinced that he will bring additional creativity to our attacking play. Furthermore, Kastriot and Mauro have already worked together very successfully. This existing connection will make his integration easier and is another building block that will enable him to contribute his qualities to the team quickly."
